subject: Urgent: streaming payload gaps causing order misses (WebSocket/chunked timeouts)
messages:
From: Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@fastpay.com>
To: hannah_schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: FastPay SRE <sre@fastpay.com>, tom.r@fastpay.com
Date: Mon, 03 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: [Urgent] Streaming drops during peak window

Hannah —

We started seeing a recurring class of failures this morning around 08:30 PT where streaming responses simply stop delivering chunks for ~8-20s and then either resume or end with a 504. This is happening on our live trading path (production) and caused a handful of missed orders.

Symptoms:
- ~22% of streaming responses observe a "payload gap" mid-response where there is silence for >8s.
- When the gap occurs, client eventually receives WS close or chunked-encoding end-of-stream with status 504.
- Errors spike during our batch arrival at 08:00-09:00 (high concurrency from 2k->6k concurrent streams).

We've attached a small pcap and a short trace of the HTTP/WebSocket session (pcap_stream_trace.txt). Can you triage urgently? We need either a mitigation path or a rollback timeline.

Alyssa
Alyssa Chen
Lead Platform Engineer, FastPay
alyssa.chen@fastpay.com

Alyssa — thanks for the quick heads-up and the pcap. I’m escalating this immediately to our SRE and runtime teams (cc).

Immediate asks:
- Can you confirm whether you were using the streaming API over WebSocket or chunked HTTP for the affected sessions? Your pcap shows WS handshake but please confirm client settings (keepalive interval, max idle).
- If possible, please switch a small percentage (5%) of traffic to non-streaming / short-polling as a temporary mitigation — I can help with the config.
- We’d like to stand up a 30-minute bridge now to run live traces and coordinate mitigation. I’m available at :35.

We’ll prioritize an emergency rollback path if a recent runtime change is implicated.

—Hannah

From: marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: hannah_schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@fastpay.com>
Cc: rachel_kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, dev_patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 03 Aug 2026 09:41:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Urgent: streaming payload gaps causing order misses (WebSocket/chunked timeouts)

Alyssa / team — initial triage notes below (from logs attached: redwood_logs_20260803.tar.gz). I pushed a short-run trace to INF-7142.

Observations:
- Error spike correlates with two things: increased concurrent streams and a soft rollout of redwood-v1.2-quant that happened 07:50 PT in the us-west cluster.
- The runtime currently uses a per-connection chunk-aggregation window of 12s; when the kernel scheduling/starvation occurs under high concurrency, the aggregation produces delayed chunk emission and client-experienced "silence".
- WebSocket pings are set at 30s by default; clients that rely on shorter keepalives (<=10s) experience a perceived stall before application-layer heartbeat detects it.

Short-term mitigations (can be applied in minutes):
1) Roll traffic to redwood-v1.1-stable (previous model) for affected routes — safe rollback, requires ~2 minutes to route change.
2) Reduce chunk-aggregation window to 3s for streaming routes to flush partial chunks sooner.
3) Force WS keepalive to 15s for connections to reduce perceived silence for clients; we can advertise a client-side header for this.

I’m attaching logs snippet in redwood_logs_20260803.tar.gz. Will deploy mitigation #2+3 as hotfix to the canary pool in 10m unless you veto.

Marcus Lin
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Alyssa

Date: Tue, 04 Aug 2026 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Urgent: streaming payload gaps causing order misses (WebSocket/chunked timeouts) — mitigation update

Update:
- Deployed chunk-aggregation window reduction to 3s and forced WS keepalive 15s to canary pool at 10:20 PT on 2026-08-03.
- Observed immediate improvement on canary: mid-response silence frequency dropped from ~24% -> ~3% for affected routes.
- Progressive roll to remaining pools completed by 13:10 PT. After full rollout, error-rate for streaming endpoints dropped from 8.1% to 1.8% and p95 latency improved by ~420ms.
- No rollback required; redwood-v1.2-quant remains gated pending further perf tuning.

Next steps:
- Post-mortem scheduled (INF-7142) for 2026-08-06 10:00 PT (invite sent).
- Hannah/rachel to lead exec sync tonight to confirm credits and customer impact.
- Follow-up: runtime team to add adaptive chunk windowing and a preflight header to let clients opt into shorter chunk flush intervals.

Marcus Lin
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
